problem:
Northgate Retail pays more than 200 suppliers each week through Meridian Bank, using a single bulk file. The finance team thinks of a payment as one action: upload the file, and the suppliers get paid. In practice, a payment passes through initiation, validation, processing, routing, clearing, settlement and confirmation, and each stage has its own owner, its own status, and its own failure mode. When a supplier calls to say they were not paid, the finance team cannot say which stage failed, because they only ever saw the file acknowledgement.

The confusion has real consequences. A file acknowledgement is treated as proof that every supplier was paid, so a rejected item is not chased until the supplier complains. A payment accepted by the bank is treated as settled, so a later clearing rejection catches the team by surprise. A returned payment is treated as a cancellation, so the original payment record is questioned instead of the return being handled as a new linked event. The team needs a workflow map that separates each stage and names the evidence that proves it.

The case follows one bulk file from initiation to confirmation, showing where each stage can fail, what status it produces, and how the team proves the outcome without guessing.
solution:
Map the workflow as seven stages with a defined status and a defined evidence artefact at each stage. Initiation captures the instruction with a unique reference, idempotency key and remittance data. Validation checks schema, mandatory fields, limits, account state and sanctions screening, and produces an item level outcome for every transaction. Processing enriches the instruction, reserves funds where the product requires it, and routes it by rail, currency, value and cut-off. Routing selects the clearing path and the intermediary chain from effective dated reference data. Clearing sends the interbank message and waits for acceptance or rejection. Settlement moves funds between accounts at the central bank or through correspondent accounts. Confirmation updates the customer status and the statement only when the authoritative settlement or clearing evidence arrives.

Keep the statuses distinct at every stage. Channel acceptance means the bank received a valid instruction. Payment engine acceptance means it passed validation. Clearing acceptance means the next agent accepted the interbank message. Settlement finality means the funds moved irrevocably. A return after settlement is a new linked event, recorded with the original references, not an erasure of the original payment. A partial batch failure is handled item by item: valid items proceed where partial processing is permitted, rejected items receive an item level reason, and accepted items are never resubmitted when rejected items are repaired.

Reconcile at the end of the workflow, not in the middle of it. The ledger, the clearing acknowledgements and the customer statements are joined by payment reference and correlation ID, and any item without a matching outcome in all three sits in an exception worklist. The workflow is complete only when every transaction has a final status that is proven by evidence, not when the file was uploaded.

decision.question: Northgate Retail uploads a bulk supplier file and receives a file acknowledgement. A supplier later says they were not paid. What does the acknowledgement actually prove?

options.label: A
options.detail: That no further checking is needed.

options.label: B
options.detail: That every supplier in the file was paid.

options.label: C
options.detail: That the file was received and passed file-level checks. Each transaction still needs its own validation, processing, clearing and settlement outcome.

options.label: D
options.detail: That the money has settled in every supplier account.

decisionRationale: C is correct because file-level acceptance and transaction-level acceptance are separate. The acknowledgement proves receipt and file-level checks only. B and A are wrong because acceptance is not settlement, and a clearing rejection or a return can still follow. A is wrong because each transaction needs its own outcome and reconciliation.

steps.title: Creates a bulk supplier file with one instruction per supplier and uploads it
Acknowledges receipt of the file and validates the file structure and control totals
Validates each transaction for schema, mandatory fields, limits, account state and screening
Enriches accepted instructions, reserves funds where required, and selects the rail and route
Sends each accepted payment as an interbank message to clearing
Accepts or rejects each message and returns a status for each item
Settles accepted payments by moving funds between settlement accounts
Posts the debit and credit entries once settlement or clearing evidence is confirmed
Updates the customer status and statement for each transaction from the authoritative outcome
Reconciles ledger, clearing and statement records for every item and clears exceptions

happy: The file is acknowledged, every transaction passes validation, each accepted payment clears and settles, the ledger posts match the clearing acknowledgements, and the customer sees a final confirmed status per supplier with a statement entry to match. Rejected items, if any, carry an item level reason and are repaired without resubmitting accepted items.

negative.title: Partial batch failure
negative.detail: Some transactions fail validation while others pass. Apply item level outcomes under the agreed partial processing rule, return reasons per item, and never resubmit accepted items.

negative.title: Clearing rejection after acceptance
negative.detail: The bank accepted the instruction but clearing rejects the interbank message. Move the payment to a defined rejected state, reverse or release any reservation once, and notify the channel with the mapped reason.

negative.title: Return after settlement
negative.detail: The beneficiary bank returns a payment after it settled. Treat the return as a new linked event with the original references, post it separately, and update the customer status.

negative.title: File control sum mismatch
negative.detail: The file total does not match the sum of its transactions. Reject the file at intake, tell the customer the exact mismatch, and do not process any item from it.

negative.title: Duplicate file
negative.detail: The same file is uploaded twice. Detect the duplicate by file ID and control totals, return the original outcomes, and do not reprocess the items.

technical: Give every file a file ID and every transaction a transaction ID, instruction ID, end to end ID and correlation ID, and carry those identifiers through every stage so any item can be traced from upload to settlement. Keep file-level and transaction-level acceptance as separate states with separate evidence. Validate against effective dated reference data for routing, limits and screening, and record which version governed each decision. Use idempotency keys at intake so a duplicate file or a retried instruction returns the original outcome. Store status transitions with timestamps and the authoritative source for each transition, and make status consumers idempotent so an out-of-order event cannot regress a payment.

messages.title: Customer credit transfer initiation, one per supplier, carrying the bulk file and item references.
Customer payment status report giving item level outcomes for the file.
Customer credit transfer sent to clearing for each accepted payment.
Payment status report confirming clearing acceptance or rejection per item.
Payment return, used when a settled payment is returned by the beneficiary side.
Bank to customer statement evidencing the final ledger postings.

accounting: The ledger posts one entry per settled payment, or one aggregate entry plus item level detail where batch booking is the agreed product, and in either case the aggregate and the item totals must reconcile. A clearing rejection releases or reverses any reservation exactly once. A return after settlement is a separate linked entry, so the original debit and the return credit both remain visible. Fees are posted as separate entries with their own references. The daily reconciliation joins the file, the clearing acknowledgements and the ledger, and any item without a matching outcome in all three sits in an exception worklist with an owner and an ageing SLA.

scenarios.given: a partially valid file and partial processing enabled
scenarios.then: each transaction receives an independent outcome. only accepted transactions proceed

scenarios.given: a clearing rejection correlated to a payment
scenarios.then: the payment is moved to the appropriate rejected state. any related accounting reservation is handled once
the return is recorded as a linked transaction. the original record remains immutable

questions.question: What does a file acknowledgement prove?
options: The file was received and passed file-level checks. Transaction outcomes are still to come
questions.explanation: File-level and transaction-level acceptance are separate. The acknowledgement proves receipt, not payment.

questions.question: A payment is accepted by the bank but rejected by clearing. What is its state?
options: Rejected at clearing, with any reservation reversed or released once and the channel notified
questions.explanation: Channel acceptance, engine acceptance, clearing acceptance and settlement are distinct states. A clearing rejection moves the payment to a defined rejected state.

questions.question: A settled payment is returned by the beneficiary bank. How is it recorded?
options: By editing the original amount to zero
As a new linked event with the original references, keeping the original record immutable
questions.explanation: A return is a separate financial event linked to the original. The original record must remain immutable for audit and reconciliation.

questions.question: In a partial batch failure, what happens to accepted items when rejected items are repaired?
options: They are not resubmitted. Only rejected items are repaired and reprocessed
They are resubmitted with the repairs
questions.explanation: Accepted items already have an outcome. Resubmitting them would duplicate payments. Only rejected items go through repair.
